proves.claim: An old release unpacks even when tar stops reading early.

git.archive.early-tar-stop.why: An old release failed to unpack when tar stopped reading early.

proves.claim: Private flake evidence keeps real bytes and refuses source paths and symlinks.

git.flakes.private-evidence.why: Private flake evidence leaked source paths or symlinks.

proves.claim: Code provenance strips inherited GIT_DIR in both worktree-to-main directions.

git.main.provenance-strips-git-dir.why: Inherited GIT_DIR misled code provenance between worktree and main.

proves.claim: Code provenance is cached per request and refreshes for the next request.

git.main.provenance-cached.why: Provenance was recomputed within one request or stale on the next.

proves.claim: resolveRevs spawns git once for HEAD, HEAD^, trunk and the merge base.

git.memo-revs.single-spawn.why: resolveRevs spawned git once per revision.

proves.claim: A repeated resolveRevs call and a repeated first-parent log read each spawn at most once.

git.memo-revs.repeat-reads.why: A repeated revision or first-parent log read spawned git again.

proves.claim: A commit already in the clone gets a detached worktree without git fetch.

git.review-folder.no-fetch.why: A commit already in the clone was fetched again.

proves.claim: A second call for the same commit reuses that folder instead of creating another.

git.review-folder.reuse.why: A second call for one commit made another folder.

proves.claim: linkedDependencies names each node_modules entry that resolves outside the review folder.

git.review-folder-deps.outside-links.why: A review folder read dependencies from outside the commit under review.

proves.claim: The same read-only git call run twice through the memo spawns git once.

git.memo.read-twice-once.why: A repeated read-only git call spawned git twice.

proves.claim: A git write through the memo clears it.

git.memo.write-clears.why: A git write left a stale memoized read.

proves.claim: A different folder or arguments never share a result.

git.memo.folder-args-separate.why: Different folders or arguments shared a memoized result.

proves.claim: No test under packages/git/tests imports a module of the CLI fixture kit.

git.kit-home.no-kit-imports.why: A git test imported a CLI fixture kit module.

proves.claim: The same tree gives the same fingerprint, with or without .git, and a dirty file moves it.

git.definition.same-tree-same-print.why: A fingerprint differed for the same tree, or ignored a dirty file.

proves.claim: An untracked file the checker loads is part of the fingerprint.

git.definition.untracked-loaded-file.why: An untracked file the checker loads was left out of the fingerprint.

proves.claim: The git index of the checkout Pullboard runs from names its clean files by blob id, and a change there moves the fingerprint.

git.definition.index-blob-ids.why: The checkout index did not name clean files by blob id.

proves.claim: Import edges are saved by blob id in the git directory for the next command.

git.definition.edges-saved-by-blob.why: Import edges were not saved by blob id for the next command.

proves.claim: The bounded look-back before each literal reads every source in the git cell the same as the whole prefix.

git.definition.lookback-bounded.why: The bounded look-back read sources differently from the whole prefix.

proves.claim: The bounded look-back scans a long file to the same result as the whole prefix and in less time.

git.definition.lookback-walk.why: A look-back that reads the whole prefix is quadratic in file length, so the walk slows as files grow.

proves.claim: A concatenated module load leaves a runner closure intact and a strict scan opaque.

git.definition.concatenated-load.why: A concatenated module load broke a runner closure.

proves.claim: The in-process Git gives the same statuses, ids and diff names as real Git for init, commit, branch, switch, merge, rev-parse and diff.

git.stand-in.journey-sequence.why: The in-process Git drifted from real Git on the common journey.

proves.claim: The stand-in refuses what it does not model and never guesses a clock.

git.stand-in.journey-bounds.why: The stand-in guessed at what it does not model.

proves.claim: The in-process Git gives the same statuses and output as real Git for worktree add and list, remote add and get-url, and rev-parse --git-common-dir.

git.stand-in.linked-worktrees-remotes.why: The stand-in drifted from real Git on linked worktrees and remotes.

proves.claim: Plain retained trunk reads avoid Git; ambiguous configuration still asks Git.

git.adapter.retained-trunk-reads.why: Retained trunk reads spawned git when they need not.

proves.claim: In-memory Git rejects uncontracted operations without real-process fallback.

git.adapter.in-memory-rejects.why: The in-memory Git fell back to a real process for an uncontracted operation.

proves.claim: Async and nested Git implementations isolate caches and restore after failure.

git.adapter.caches-isolated.why: Async or nested Git implementations shared caches or kept them after failure.

proves.claim: Git transport preserves caller arguments, stdin and bounds at the migrated seam.

git.adapter.transport-preserves.why: Git transport changed caller arguments, stdin or bounds.

proves.claim: Real Git streaming implementation preserves child output and completion.

git.adapter.streaming-real.why: Real Git streaming lost child output or completion.

proves.claim: Literal Git launch ratchet counts code and aliases, rejects growth, and reports the remaining migration.

git.adapter.launch-ratchet.why: The launch ratchet miscounted or allowed growth.

proves.claim: The Git launch scan counts package launchers at their true path and fails a planted one naming the file.

git.adapter.launch-scan-paths.why: The launch scan missed a planted launcher or misnamed its file.

proves.claim: The committed Git launch allowance names only files that still launch Git at that path.

git.adapter.allowance-names-launchers.why: The allowance named files that no longer launch Git.

proves.claim: No direct Git launch exceeds the committed allowance and the allowance stays within its original total.

git.adapter.no-launch-over-allowance.why: A direct Git launch exceeded the committed allowance.

proves.claim: repoInfo, codeIsFromMain, headCommit and headTree answer from cache with no Git process after .git directory churn.

git.adapter.cache-after-churn.why: repoInfo and head reads spawned Git after .git directory churn.

proves.claim: A moved HEAD ref still refreshes headCommit.

git.adapter.head-ref-moves.why: A moved HEAD ref did not refresh headCommit.

proves.claim: every git-cell test registered here has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only with tests.registryStrict on.

git.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: Every git test file that reads files carries an input header naming the cells it reads.

git.inputs.every-reader-declares-its-inp.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: Every git test header is a non-empty declaration.

git.inputs.every-header-is-a-non-empty-d.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: A second fingerprint of a 300-module checker reads saved edges, gives the same result and takes less time than the first.

git.definition-warm.saved-edges-faster.why: Without saved edges every submit re-reads every module the checker loads.

proves.claim: The real adapter spawns the first PATH git that is not the shim, else the xcrun answer, resolved once per process.

git.adapter.real-path-resolution.why: Without it every git call goes through the shim and pays two execs.

proves.claim: A failed or empty git resolution falls back to plain git.

git.adapter.real-path-fallback.why: Without it a missing xcrun or empty answer would spawn nothing.

proves.claim: lockfileCacheKey returns one key for identical package-lock.json bytes and another when one byte differs.

git.review-folder-cache.key-follows-lock.why: Without it the review folder dependency cache could be keyed by something other than the lockfile bytes.

proves.claim: lockfileCacheKey refuses naming package-lock.json when the folder has no lockfile.

git.review-folder-cache.no-lockfile-refu.why: Without it the review folder dependency cache could be keyed by something other than the lockfile bytes.
